note: Every claim published on this site points at one of these. 'tier' records how strong the source is: primary = the authoritative body itself (Amazon's own agreement/policies, a .gov agency, Google Search Central, the product listing itself); supplied = provided by the site owner and not independently corroborated.

sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
supports: Section 5 requires the exact or substantially similar statement: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases." and forbids implying Amazon endorses you.
A violation of Section 5 is a material breach (Section 6).

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (updated April 14, 2026)
supports: Section 2(a): Special Links must use the assigned Associates ID.
Section 2(b): links must not obscure that the destination is an Amazon Site; a link-shortening service used so the destination is unclear is prohibited.
Section 2(b): prices and availability may be shown only if Amazon serves that data or it comes via the Product Advertising / Creators API.
Section 2(b): no inaccurate, overbroad or misleading claims about a Product.
Section 2(b): Product lists (search results, department pages) require additional original content on the site.

sources.title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers
supports: Disclose any financial, employment, personal or family relationship with a brand.
The disclosure must be hard to miss and placed with the endorsement itself, not only on an about page or at the end.
"advertisement", "ad" and "sponsored" are acceptable plain terms.
"You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried."

sources.title: Endorsements, Influencers, and Reviews (guidance hub)
supports: The Endorsement Guides apply to reviews and endorsements; the hub links the Guides, staff FAQs and business guidance.

sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
sources.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart (last updated April 14, 2025)
supports: Beef, pork, veal and lamb steaks, chops and roasts: 145 °F (62.8 °C) and rest at least 3 minutes.
Ground meats: 160 °F (71.1 °C). All poultry: 165 °F (73.9 °C). Fish and shellfish: 145 °F (62.8 °C). Leftovers and casseroles: 165 °F (73.9 °C).
"Cook all food to these minimum internal temperatures, as measured with a food thermometer, before removing food from the heat source."

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google (last updated 2025-12-10)
supports: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements with rel="sponsored".
Multiple rel values may be supplied as a space- or comma-separated list.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search — thin affiliation, scaled content abuse, misleading functionality
supports: "Thin affiliation" is listed as a spam policy: affiliate pages that lack original value can be demoted or removed.
"Scaled content abuse" covers producing content at scale primarily to manipulate rankings.

sources.title: Control your snippets in search results — best practices for meta descriptions
supports: "Create unique descriptions for each page on your site"; identical descriptions on every page are called out as a problem.
A meta description is used when it describes the page better than on-page text.

sources.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
supports: The content and quality self-assessment questions (original analysis, completeness, insight beyond the obvious, descriptive headings).
E-E-A-T and the "Who, How, Why" test for authorship and purpose.
